claims.text: Topiramate can cause hyperchloremic, non-anion gap metabolic acidosis (renal bicarbonate loss from carbonic anhydrase inhibition);
claims.quote: TOPAMAX can cause hyperchloremic, non-anion gap, metabolic acidosis (i.e., decreased serum bicarbonate below the normal reference range in the absence of chronic respiratory alkalosis). This metabolic acidosis is caused by renal bicarbonate loss due to carbonic anhydrase inhibition by TOPAMAX.

claims.text: measure serum bicarbonate at baseline and periodically, and if acidosis persists consider reducing the dose or stopping (with a taper).
claims.quote: Measurement of baseline and periodic serum bicarbonate during topiramate treatment is recommended. If metabolic acidosis develops and persists, consideration should be given to reducing the dose or discontinuing TOPAMAX (using dose tapering).

claims.text: Acute myopia with secondary angle-closure glaucoma: can cause permanent visual loss; stop topiramate as soon as possible.
claims.quote: Acute myopia and secondary angle closure glaucoma: can lead to permanent visual loss; discontinue TOPAMAX as soon as possible

claims.text: Metabolic acidosis: baseline and periodic serum bicarbonate recommended.
claims.quote: Metabolic acidosis: baseline and periodic measurement of serum bicarbonate is recommended

claims.text: Fetal toxicity: major congenital malformations in pregnancy, including cleft lip and/or palate.
claims.quote: Fetal Toxicity: use during pregnancy can cause major congenital malformations, including but not limited to cleft lip and/or palate
